div.head: Leis Wl 24
div.ab: De hume ki plaided en curt, en ki curt que ceo seit, fors la u le cors le rei seit, e hom lui met sure, k'il ad dit chose, qu'il ne voille conuistre, s'il pot derehdner par un entendable hume del plait oant e veant, qu'il ne l'averad dit, recovré ad sa parole.

Home qui plaide en curt, a qui curt que ço seit, fors la ou le cors le rei est, e home li mettid sur, qu'il ait dit chose, que il ne voille conustre, se il ne pot derainer per II entendable home del plei[t o]ant et veant, que il ne l'avrad dit, recovered a sa parole. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

Si quis negat in curia se dixisse quod ei imponitur. In omni curia preterquam in presentia regis, si cui imponitur, quod in placito dixerit aliquid, quod ipse negat se dixisse, nisi possit per duos intelligibiles homines de auditu conuincere, recuperabit ad loquelam suam.

De hume ki plaided en curt, en ki curt que ceo seit, fors la u le cors le rei seit, e hom lui met sure k'il ad dit chose qu'il ne voille conuistre, s'il pot derehdner par un entendable hume del plait oant e veant qu'il ne l'averad dit, recovré ad sa parole.

24. Betreffend jemanden, der im Gerichte processirt — in wessen Gericht es auch sei, ausser da, wo des Königs Person ist —: gesetzt es wird [dorther Record] gegen ihn geltend gemacht, dass er [dort] etwas gesagt habe, was er nicht anerkennen will, wenn er durch eine glaubwürdige Person (2 Pernen IL) jenes Processes als Ohren- und Augenzeugen nachweisen kann, dass er es nicht gesagt habe, so hat er [jenes] sein Wort hergestellt [gebessert].

24. Concerning someone who pleads in court — in whosesoever court it may be, except where the king's person is —: supposing it is alleged against him [by record from there] that he said something [there] which he will not acknowledge, if he can prove by one credible person (2 persons IL) of that suit, as witness by ear and eye, that he did not say it, then he has restored [amended] [that] word of his.

When a man carries on a suit in any court other than that in which the king is present in person, and it is maintained against him that he has said something which he will not acknowledge—if he can prove by means of a trustworthy man, who has seen and heard all the suit, that he did not say it, then the validity of his word shall be admitted.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 266–267 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 510–511, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)
